currentContext.expansion: The Company has activated a new Real Estate business segment (in addition to its existing single-property Hospitality business at Chembur, Mumbai) and has invested Rs.35.61 crores in this segment as on 31st March 2026. It has received an LOI for its Chembur real estate project and is gearing up to kick-start operations in the coming months, expecting to receive all necessary approvals and start the project by Q3 of the current financial year while securing financial closure for funding. A second project at Mahim is under consolidation phase and is expected to start within the current financial year. The Company continues to follow its growth targets in line with an asset-light expansion strategy, and is also exploring expansion of its existing hospitality business by adding new/modern facilities and increasing capacity of existing facilities.

risks.note: The Company operates out of its single standalone hospitality property located at Chembur, Mumbai, with no other operating property disclosed, exposing revenue to single-site/single-market concentration.

The Real Estate segment was only activated in FY2025-26 and recorded no revenue for the year; the Chembur project has received only an LOI while the Mahim project remains under consolidation, so approvals, funding (financial closure) and start-up timelines for both are still pending.

Management explicitly notes that the business continues to be influenced by the global geopolitical situation, overall economic growth, tourism trends and general business sentiment prevailing in the market.

risks.risk: Broad regulatory, tax and litigation risk
risks.note: The cautionary statement flags slowdown in India's economic growth, inflation, war, changes in Government Regulations and tax laws, and factors such as litigation and labour relations as risks that could cause actual results to differ from forward-looking statements.

risks.risk: Liquidity and credit risk amid continuing losses
risks.note: The Board/Management continuously review strategic, operational, financial, credit, market, liquidity, legal, regulatory and cybersecurity risks under the Risk Management Policy; liquidity and credit risk are live considerations given the Company's continuing operating losses.

The Company has remained loss-making at the EBIT/PAT level; although losses narrowed year-on-year, sustained profitability is not yet demonstrated and remains dependent on hospitality demand recovery and the untested Real Estate segment.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's hospitality and tourism industry continues to benefit from increasing domestic travel, growing business activity, improved infrastructure and rising consumer spending
- Favourable market conditions enabled steady growth in occupancy levels, enhanced guest engagement and improved operational efficiencies
- India's economic growth trajectory, increasing urbanization, expanding tourism infrastructure and supportive government initiatives present significant opportunities for businesses with a long-term vision
- Growing trend of tourism, increase in disposable income and inclination of people towards wellness and leisure expected to support future prospects and enhanced revenues
- Business continues to be influenced by global geopolitical situation, overall economic growth, tourism trends and general business sentiment prevailing in the market

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Continue to strengthen position in the hospitality sector while laying the foundation for expansion into new business verticals (real estate)
- Build a well-diversified business model capable of delivering sustainable growth while navigating changing market dynamics
- Focus on operational excellence, prudent financial management, digital transformation, customer delight and sustainable growth
- Continue to focus on strengthening operations, improving efficiencies and developing alternate revenue streams for sustainable growth
- Committed to maintaining facilities in good condition, retaining a capable team and implementing measures to further strengthen the operational and financial position
- Exploring expansion of existing hospitality business by adding new/modern facilities and increasing capacity of existing facilities to boost revenues
- Actively working to establish new revenue streams to strengthen operations and overall financial position

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company has activated a new Real Estate business segment (in addition to its existing single-property Hospitality business at Chembur, Mumbai) and has invested Rs.35.61 crores in this segment as on 31st March 2026. It has received an LOI for its Chembur real estate project and is gearing up to kick-start operations in the coming months, expecting to receive all necessary approvals and start the project by Q3 of the current financial year while securing financial closure for funding. A second project at Mahim is under consolidation phase and is expected to start within the current financial year. The Company continues to follow its growth targets in line with an asset-light expansion strategy, and is also exploring expansion of its existing hospitality business by adding new/modern facilities and increasing capacity of existing facilities.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Strong brand goodwill and customer endorsement for its Exclusive Multi-Cuisine Pure Vegetarian restaurants and banquets
- Strategic location of operations aiding ability to capture business/leisure demand
- Loyal, skilled workforce built over decades
- Asset-light expansion strategy for growth into new revenue streams

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Single-site concentration — The Company operates out of its single standalone hospitality property located at Chembur, Mumbai, with no other operating property disclosed, exposing revenue to single-site/single-market concentration.
- New, unproven Real Estate vertical — The Real Estate segment was only activated in FY2025-26 and recorded no revenue for the year; the Chembur project has received only an LOI while the Mahim project remains under consolidation, so approvals, funding (financial closure) and start-up timelines for both are still pending.
- Macro and tourism-demand cyclicality — Management explicitly notes that the business continues to be influenced by the global geopolitical situation, overall economic growth, tourism trends and general business sentiment prevailing in the market.
- Broad regulatory, tax and litigation risk — The cautionary statement flags slowdown in India's economic growth, inflation, war, changes in Government Regulations and tax laws, and factors such as litigation and labour relations as risks that could cause actual results to differ from forward-looking statements.
- Liquidity and credit risk amid continuing losses — The Board/Management continuously review strategic, operational, financial, credit, market, liquidity, legal, regulatory and cybersecurity risks under the Risk Management Policy; liquidity and credit risk are live considerations given the Company's continuing operating losses.
- Continuing operating losses — The Company has remained loss-making at the EBIT/PAT level; although losses narrowed year-on-year, sustained profitability is not yet demonstrated and remains dependent on hospitality demand recovery and the untested Real Estate segment.
